Prevention: Use clean pasture seed to reduce the chance of contamination
Avoid movement of livestock through infested areas to prevent spread of seed
Prevent water runoff from infested land to non-infested land
Maintain a regular weeding regime before the plants grow big in order to facilitate uprooting
Prosopis from roadsides, wastelands, field boundaries and other areas that serve as source of infestation
Monitoring: Perennial,woody shrub 3-5m or tree growing up to 15m height.
Bark rough grey-green, becomes scaly with age.
Often multi-stemmed, especially following cutbacks, with abundant large and very sharp thorns (up to 5cm).
Leaves doubly-divided composed (6-8cm long), 12-25 pairs of oblong leaflets per leaf.
Flowers fragrant golden-yellow, dense spikes about 5-10cm long.
Fruits cylindrical or slightly irregularly curved green pods which turns yellow upon ripening (10-20cm long) containing 10-20 hard oval or elliptic, brown seeds
Regularly check edges of waterbodies, grazing areas and animal gathering areas and consider direct control if present
Check for growth of trees where there are animal dropping/dungs since seeds pass through animal dungs and germinate
Check fields for infestation and consider direct control during when observed in the field
Direct Control: Hand pulling is effective on seedlings up to 20cm in height
Cutting is effective before seed production.
Application of glyphosate to the cut stump may prevent re- sprouting
Uprooting trees or cutting 10-15cm below ground to remove crown in order to prevent coppices
Follow up weeding consistently to achieve longer term control
Glyphosate (6l/ha) can be used as a spot treatment to prevent re-sprouting after cutting the stumps
Apply 2,4 -D amine, at 2l/ ha foliar application to actively growing seedlings
Tordon (Picloram 65g/l + 2,4-D 240g/l) mixed with diesel using low pressure sprayer targeting the stump to kill the roots
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, and pre-harvest interval
U (unlikely to present acute hazard under normal use)); 2,4-D WHO class
